page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is a memory-oriented general-purpose virtual machine designed to deliver a high memory-to-compute ratio on cost-efficient architecture. It operates on 64-bit x86 hardware utilizing AMD EPYC 7B12 processors. The configuration provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. The system features 64 GB of RAM, establishing an allocation of 8 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included, and no local storage is bundled with the instance.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate distinct performance characteristics across varied workloads. The instance achieves strong results in stress-ng single-core testing, ranking in the top quartile with a score of 2681.48. Multi-core performance aligns with the median tier, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 10764.32 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5778. Memory throughput delivers steady performance across cached and uncached blocks, sustaining 69.61 GB/sec on large uncached reads and 46.34 GB/sec on large uncached writes. Database and key-value throughput is highlighted by 7.66 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.24 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and extended instruction benchmarks exhibit weaker relative results, consistent with the omission of AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

The configuration presents notable architectural tradeoffs. The absence of local NVMe storage and included public IPv4 addresses necessitates external block storage and network provisioning. Furthermore, workloads reliant on advanced matrix math or extensive SIMD instructions will see reduced throughput compared to newer microarchitectures. Nevertheless, the substantial 64 GB memory capacity provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-constrained workloads without requiring higher-tier compute pricing. The instance is suited for in-memory key-value databases, caching infrastructure like Redis, enterprise backend applications, mid-tier data transformation pipelines, and memory-heavy web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance configured with an elevated 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor, it supplies 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores alongside 64 GB of system RAM, allocating 8 GB of memory per core. The instance includes hardware support for AES, SHA-NI, and AVX instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions and bundled GPU acceleration. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external block storage for persistent data. Synthetic benchmarks show strong single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng alongside middle-tier multi-core computing and memory bandwidth figures, including 7.66 million Redis SET operations per second. However, heavy vector compute and multi-threaded decompression tests reveal lower relative throughput due to instruction limitations. Balancing large memory capacity against moderate compute density, this instance profile provides cost-efficient scaling for in-memory data stores, Redis caches, ETL pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise services.
